newsitem.title: USA: Maine Gov proposes $433 mln budget for highways.
newsitem.headline: Maine Gov proposes $433 mln budget for highways.

text.p: Maine Governor Angus King on Monday proposed a $433.1 million budget for fiscal year 1998-1999, down approximately $21 million from the previous budget.

King noted that the state was accelerating its capital program and avoiding an increase in the gasoline tax even though revenues for the highway fund are expected to fall about $11 million to $429.5 million.

The new budget would maintain the current levels of staffing, but shift some payroll expenses. Salaries for district attorneys no longer will be provided by the Highway Fund as they have been for the past six years, while only 60 percent of state police expenses will be paid by it, down from 88 percent in 1994.
The new budget matches an estimated $170 million in federal funds over the biennium.

King said that the Department of Transportation's capital program would be proposed in more detail in February, adding resurfacing of highways and replacement and repair of state and local bridges will be its highest priorities.

The budget calls for a 50 percent rise in funding for the Local Bridge Program, which helps towns replace or repair local bridges. And the Local Roads Assistance Program will be fully funded. The state said it will pave 2,800 miles from 1995 to 1998, up 21 percent from the previous three-year period.
